sentences.en: Thanks to the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation for underwriting this special two-part series
sentences.zh: 感谢罗伯特·伍德·约翰逊基金会资助本期两集特别节目，

sentences.en: about the power of sound to affect and influence our health and well-being.
sentences.zh: 探讨声音对我们的健康和福祉产生影响和作用的力量。

sentences.en: The Robert Wood Johnson Foundation is working alongside others to build a culture of health
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·伍德·约翰逊基金会正与各方携手，

sentences.en: for everyone in America.
sentences.zh: 为全美每一个人构建健康文化。

sentences.en: Learn more about them at rwjf.org.
sentences.zh: 请访问 rwjf.org 了解更多信息。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Sound can have serious impacts on our health and well-being.
sentences.zh: 声音会对我们的健康和福祉产生严重的影响。

sentences.en: And ever since people moved into cities, we have been exposed to an unhealthy amount of noise.
sentences.zh: 自从人类搬进城市以来，我们就一直暴露在不健康的噪声量中。

sentences.en: Cars, power lines, and the constant ding of our devices.
sentences.zh: 汽车、电线，以及我们各种电子设备的不断哔哔声。

sentences.en: We live in a very noisy world.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个非常嘈杂的世界里。

sentences.en: And most of the noises we hear aren't designed to work together.
sentences.zh: 而且我们听到的大多数声音都不是为了协同工作而设计的。

sentences.en: This is the second part of our special series on sound and health,
sentences.zh: 这是我们关于声音与健康的特别节目的第二部分，

sentences.en: supported by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation.
sentences.zh: 由罗伯特·伍德·约翰逊基金会赞助。

sentences.en: We're taking a look at how a more intentional approach to sound can help us live better, healthier lives.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨更有意识地对待声音的方法如何帮助我们过上更好、更健康的生活。

sentences.en: And there's no better place to think about health than hospitals.
sentences.zh: 没有比医院更适合思考健康问题的地方了。

sentences.en: Joe Schlesinger is an anesthesiologist at Vanderbilt Medical Center.
sentences.zh: 乔·施莱辛格是范德堡医学中心的麻醉师。

sentences.en: He spends a lot of his time in the operating room.
sentences.zh: 他大部分时间都在手术室里度过。

sentences.en: The operating room is an interesting space because we think of it, it's like my cockpit, if you will.
sentences.zh: 手术室是一个很有意思的空间，因为我们认为它就像我的驾驶舱，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: And anesthesiology is related a lot to aviation.
sentences.zh: 而且麻醉学与航空业有很多相似之处。

sentences.en: We are a culture of safety.
sentences.zh: 我们崇尚安全文化。

sentences.en: We have safety checklists just like pilots do.
sentences.zh: 我们有和飞行员一样的安全检查清单。

sentences.en: We think of takeoff and landing, just like putting a patient to sleep and waking them up.
sentences.zh: 我们会想到起飞和降落，就像让病人入睡和唤醒他们一样。

sentences.en: In fact, when we wake someone up from anesthesia, we call it landing the plane.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我们把某人从麻醉中唤醒时，我们称之为“降落飞机”。

sentences.en: Landing the plane takes focus, but Joe doesn't work in silence.
sentences.zh: 降落飞机需要集中注意力，但乔并不是在安静环境中工作的。

sentences.en: It might come as a surprise, but in the OR, there's music playing all the time.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让人感到意外，但在手术室里，总是有音乐在播放。

sentences.en: There's great data that shows that music improves surgical efficiency,
sentences.zh: 有大量的数据表明，音乐可以提高手术效率，

sentences.en: which can translate to an economic benefit.
sentences.zh: 这可以转化为经济效益。

sentences.en: And music subjectively makes us feel good.
sentences.zh: 而且音乐在主观上能让我们感觉良好。

sentences.en: And if you're working long hours doing difficult cases in the operating room,
sentences.zh: 如果你在手术室里长时间工作、处理棘手的病例，

sentences.en: if you can improve mood, certainly there's benefit.
sentences.zh: 如果你能改善心情，这肯定是有好处的。

sentences.en: But who chooses the music is usually the surgeon.
sentences.zh: 但选择音乐的人通常是外科医生。

sentences.en: And if the surgeon's excited the surgery's over and the music volume gets cranked up,
sentences.zh: 如果外科医生因为手术结束而兴奋，把音乐音量开得很大，

sentences.en: it's really hard for us to be delicate and intentional and artful and elegant about our anesthetic.
sentences.zh: 我们就很难对我们的麻醉做到细腻、刻意、艺术和优雅。

sentences.en: Joe remembers one surgery where music was playing,
sentences.zh: 乔记得有一次手术，当时正播放着音乐，

sentences.en: and then all of a sudden, the patient's vital signs started to crash.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，病人的生命体征开始崩溃。

sentences.en: And so now my alarms are going off, the music volume is high.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我的警报器在响，音乐音量很大。

sentences.en: The surgeon and I are having to raise our voices and almost yell at each other to communicate,
sentences.zh: 我和外科医生不得不提高嗓门，几乎是对着彼此大喊来沟通，

sentences.en: not because we're mad at each other, but just to understand each other.
sentences.zh: 不是因为我们生彼此的气，而只是为了听清对方。

sentences.en: So Joe and his researchers are trying to figure out how to get the benefits of music in the OR
sentences.zh: 因此，乔和他的研究人员正试图找出如何在手术室里获得音乐的好处，

sentences.en: without the risk of hearing, we built this city on rock and roll while someone is having a heart attack.
sentences.zh: 同时又不会冒着当有人心脏病发作时播放“我们靠摇滚乐建成了这座城市”的风险。

sentences.en: I'm working with another anesthesiologist on a device which is called the Canary Box.
sentences.zh: 我正与另一位麻醉师合作研制一种名为“金丝雀盒子”的设备。

sentences.en: The Canary Box has two levels of alarm, a warning zone and a danger zone.
sentences.zh: “金丝雀盒子”有两个级别的警报：警告区和危险区。

sentences.en: When the alarm is in the warning zone, it halves the music volume.
sentences.zh: 当警报处于警告区时，它会将音乐音量减半。

sentences.en: And when the alarm is in the danger zone, it turns the music off.
sentences.zh: 而当警报处于危险区时，它会关闭音乐。

sentences.en: Fixing how sounds work together in the operating room is a step in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 修复手术室中声音协同工作的方式是朝着正确方向迈出的一步。

sentences.en: But it's part of a bigger problem.
sentences.zh: 但这只是一个更大问题的一部分。

sentences.en: Doctors know more about the human body than ever and are better equipped to save your life.
sentences.zh: 医生对人体的了解比以往任何时候都多，并且更有能力拯救你的生命。

sentences.en: But still.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此。

sentences.en: Hospitals are horrible places to get better.
sentences.zh: 医院是康复的糟糕场所。

sentences.en: That's sound designer Joel Beckerman.
sentences.zh: 那是声音设计师乔尔·贝克曼。

sentences.en: And he's right.
sentences.zh: 他说得对。

sentences.en: Hospitals can be bad for your health because hospitals sound terrible.
sentences.zh: 医院对你的健康有害，因为医院听起来太糟糕了。

sentences.en: I think of when I walk into the neuro ICU and I hear the automatic door which opens and closes.
sentences.zh: 我想起当我走入神经科重症监护室时，我听到自动门开开关关。

sentences.en: As people walk by, it opens and closes without anyone going in or out.
sentences.zh: 当人们走过时，它开开关关，却没有任何人进出。

sentences.en: And as I walk in, there's the hubbub of people talking.
sentences.zh: 当我走进去时，是一片人们交谈的嘈杂声。

sentences.en: And it might be clinicians.
sentences.zh: 那可能是临床医生。

sentences.en: It might be patients' families.
sentences.zh: 那可能是病人的家属。

sentences.en: I hear the rolling of the big metal cart that houses all the meals for the patients.
sentences.zh: 我听到放置病人所有餐饮的大金属推车滚动的声音。

sentences.en: And it's the wheels rolling on the hardwood floor.
sentences.zh: 那是轮子在硬木地板上滚动的声音。

sentences.en: Yoko Sen is an electronic musician researching sound in hospitals.
sentences.zh: 横山阳子是一位研究医院声音的电子音乐家。

sentences.en: When it's quiet, it's about 40 to 50 decibels.
sentences.zh: 当它安静时，大约是 40 到 50 分贝。

sentences.en: But when it's pretty loud, it goes up to easily 60, 70 decibels.
sentences.zh: 但当它相当吵闹时，很容易上升到 60、70 分贝。

sentences.en: Sometimes it hits 80 to 90 decibels as well.
sentences.zh: 有时它甚至会达到 80 到 90 分贝。

sentences.en: To give you some perspective, 60 decibels is the volume of an average office.
sentences.zh: 为了让你有个直观的概念，60 分贝是普通办公室的音量。

sentences.en: 70 decibels is about as loud as a vacuum cleaner.
sentences.zh: 70 分贝大约和吸尘器一样响。

sentences.en: 80 decibels is as loud as a garbage disposal.
sentences.zh: 80 分贝和食物垃圾处理机一样响。

sentences.en: And 90 decibels is as loud as a motorcycle passing by.
sentences.zh: 而 90 分贝则和一辆摩托车驶过一样响。

sentences.en: All this in your so-called healing environment.
sentences.zh: 这一切都发生在你所谓的康复环境中。

sentences.en: Hospitals can be really loud.
sentences.zh: 医院可能会非常吵闹。

sentences.en: But volume isn't the only problem.
sentences.zh: 但音量并不是唯一的问题。

sentences.en: I hear alarms coming from multiple patient rooMs.
sentences.zh: 我听到来自多个病房的警报声。

sentences.en: And I don't know what's wrong with the patients.
sentences.zh: 我不知道病人们怎么了。

sentences.en: The alarms are difficult to localize, so I'm not sure which rooms they're coming from.
sentences.zh: 这些警报很难辨别方向，所以我不太确定它们是从哪个房间传出来的。

sentences.en: And even when he knows what he's listening for,
sentences.zh: 甚至当他知道自己在听什么声音时，

sentences.en: Joe has a hard time figuring out what device is making noise.
sentences.zh: 乔也很难弄清楚到底是哪个设备在发出噪声。

sentences.en: It could be the IV infusion pump, the epidural pump,
sentences.zh: 它可能是静脉输液泵、硬膜外麻醉泵、

sentences.en: the intra-aortic balloon pump, the dialysis machine, the ventilator.
sentences.zh: 主动脉内球囊反搏泵、透析机、呼吸机。

sentences.en: Joel Beckerman has experienced the same thing in hospitals he's worked in.
sentences.zh: 乔尔·贝克曼在他工作过的医院里也经历过同样的事情。

sentences.en: There's a heart monitor that makes 86 different alarMs.
sentences.zh: 有一个心脏监护仪会发出 86 种不同的警报。

sentences.en: There's no way that that can be meaningful to anybody.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不可能是对任何人都有意义的。

sentences.en: The scary thing is, most of these alarms are false alarMs.
sentences.zh: 可怕的是，这些警报大多是误报。

sentences.en: It could be due to a loose connection or a temporary blip in the patient's vital signs.
sentences.zh: 这可能是由于连接松动或病人生命体征的暂时波动造成的。

sentences.en: But most of these alarms don't tell you anything useful.
sentences.zh: 但这些警报大多没有告诉你任何有用的信息。

sentences.en: Still, they saturate the hospital soundscape.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，它们还是充斥了医院的声音景观。

sentences.en: I go home at night, and I still hear the beeping of alarms and the beeping of pulse oximetry in my head.
sentences.zh: 我晚上回家，脑海里依然能听到警报的哔哔声和脉搏血氧仪的哔哔声。

sentences.en: Clinicians are annoyed by lots of alarms, but there are a number of physicians and nurses that,
sentences.zh: 临床医生对大量的警报感到烦恼，但也有许多内科医生和护士觉得，

sentences.en: I love those alarMs.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这些警报。

sentences.en: Like, I have my adrenaline up, and I get excited.
sentences.zh: 就像，我的肾上腺素上升了，我很兴奋。

sentences.en: But the high from alarms is not sustainable.
sentences.zh: 但警报带来的兴奋感是不可持续的。

sentences.en: It's actually pretty exhausting.
sentences.zh: 实际上这相当令人精疲力竭。

sentences.en: The result is something called alarm fatigue.
sentences.zh: 其结果就是所谓的“警报疲劳”。

sentences.en: The problem with alarm fatigue is that din of sound which caregivers learn to ignore
sentences.zh: 警报疲劳的问题在于，医护人员学会忽略的那片喧闹杂音，

sentences.en: means that they also ignore critical alarms, and patients die.
sentences.zh: 意味着他们也会忽略关键警报，从而导致病人死亡。

sentences.en: This is a very, very serious problem that needs to be addressed.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常非常严重的问题，需要加以解决。

sentences.en: When things are loud, people complain that it's difficult to sleep at night.
sentences.zh: 当环境嘈杂时，人们会抱怨晚上很难入睡。

sentences.en: It disturbs their sleep.
sentences.zh: 这扰乱了他们的睡眠。

sentences.en: It disturbs their reSt.
sentences.zh: 这扰乱了他们的休息。

sentences.en: Noisy environment could cause more anxiety, sense of fear, and stress for patients.
sentences.zh: 嘈杂的环境会给患者带来更多的焦虑、恐惧感和压力。

sentences.en: And visitors as well.
sentences.zh: 探访者也是如此。

sentences.en: I often hear from those parents that when alarms go for, you know, their babies,
sentences.zh: 我经常从那些父母那里听到，当警报为，你知道的，他们的婴儿响起时，

sentences.en: the first thing that young parents would think is,
sentences.zh: 年轻父母首先想到的事情是，

sentences.en: oh no, is my baby going to die?
sentences.zh: 噢不，我的宝宝会死吗？

sentences.en: It's very scary.
sentences.zh: 这太可怕了。

sentences.en: It can lead to neuropsychological side effects such as ICU delirium.
sentences.zh: 它会导致神经心理学副作用，例如ICU谵妄。

sentences.en: ICU delirium is when patients get confused and paranoid
sentences.zh: ICU谵妄是指患者由于在医院呆得精疲力竭而

sentences.en: because of the exhaustion of staying in a hospital.
sentences.zh: 变得精神错乱和偏执。

sentences.en: Sometimes this can lead to hallucinations.
sentences.zh: 有时这会导致幻觉。

sentences.en: Up to 80% of patients in an ICU are thought to experience some form of delirium
sentences.zh: 据认为，ICU中高达 80% 的患者在住院期间会经历某种形式的谵妄。

sentences.en: during their hospital stay.
sentences.zh: 这是那种会给住院患者留下创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）的事情。

sentences.en: It's the sort of thing that can leave hospital patients with PTSD.
sentences.zh: 我采访过一个人。

sentences.en: I interviewed one person.
sentences.zh: 他的女儿，你知道的，在十多年前住过新生儿重症监护室（NICU）。

sentences.en: He had his daughter, you know, more than 10 years ago in NICU.
sentences.zh: 那是针对婴儿的新生儿重症监护室。

sentences.en: That's the NICU intensive care for infants.
sentences.zh: 当时有一个特定的警报声一直在响。

sentences.en: And there was this particular alarm sound that kept going off.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在 10 年后，如果他在电视或其他地方听到类似于那个警报的声音，

sentences.en: So even after 10 years, if he hears the sound that's similar to the alarm on television
sentences.zh: 他仍然会有这种类似创伤的反应。

sentences.en: or other places, he still gets this sort of a traumatized reaction.
sentences.zh: 它对身体和心灵都有持久的影响。

sentences.en: There are long-lasting effects on the body as well as the mind.
sentences.zh: 噪声会导致压力，体内的应激激素会使我们的血管变硬，

sentences.en: Noise leads to stress and stress hormones in the body stiffen our blood vessels,
sentences.zh: 这会增加心脏病发作的风险。

sentences.en: which can increase the risk of heart attack.
sentences.zh: 我经常引用弗洛伦斯·南丁格尔的这句话，她说，

sentences.en: I often quote this phrase from Florence Nightingale, who said,
sentences.zh: 不必要的噪声是对护理最残忍的缺失。

sentences.en: unnecessary noise is the cruelest absence of care.
sentences.zh: 她在 100 多年前就写下了这句话。

sentences.en: And she wrote that more than 100 years ago.
sentences.zh: 但我猜 100 年前并不存在警报疲劳这个问题。

sentences.en: But I'm guessing 100 years ago, there was no alarm fatigue as an issue.
sentences.zh: 医学中的大多数事物在 100 年里都取得了进步。

sentences.en: Most things in medicine progressed in 100 years.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，当谈到我们声音环境的质量时，

sentences.en: But I feel like when it comes to the quality of our sound environment,
sentences.zh: 这就好比我们技术进步的一个副作用。

sentences.en: it's like a side effect of our technological advancement.
sentences.zh: 所以我敢说事情变得更吵了。

sentences.en: So I bet things got louder.
sentences.zh: 现在，你无法把警报调小声。

sentences.en: Right now, you can't turn alarms softer.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它们静音。

sentences.en: You can silence them.
sentences.zh: 但美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）维护的一个数据库发现，将近 600 名患者

sentences.en: But the FDA maintained a database which found that nearly 600 patients had adverse outcomes,
sentences.zh: 因为警报管理不善而产生了不良后果，主要是死亡。

sentences.en: mostly death, from alarm mismanagement.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将讨论如何让医院警报的声音设计

sentences.en: Right now, we'll talk about how we can make the sound design of hospital alarms
sentences.zh: 变得像发出这些警报的医疗设备一样复杂和精确，广告之后见。

sentences.en: as sophisticated and precise as the medical devices that are blaring them out after this.
sentences.zh: 对这档探索声音影响健康力量的两集特别节目的支持

sentences.en: Support for this special two-part series exploring the power of sound to influence our health
sentences.zh: 来自罗伯特·伍德·约翰逊基金会。

sentences.en: comes from the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·伍德·约翰逊基金会致力于构建健康文化，

sentences.en: The Robert Wood Johnson Foundation is working to build a culture of health
sentences.zh: 确保美国每个人都拥有公平公正的健康和福祉机会，

sentences.en: that ensures everyone in America has a fair and just opportunity for health and well-being,
sentences.zh: 其中包括探讨我们当前或未来的环境将如何影响日常生活。

sentences.en: which includes exploring how our current or future environments will impact daily life.
sentences.zh: 请访问 rwjf.org 了解更多信息。

sentences.en: Learn more at rwjf.org.
sentences.zh: 当你想到病人监护仪或任何设备的设计时，

sentences.en: When you think of the design of a patient monitor or any device,
sentences.zh: 你会想到设备的视觉复杂性和设备的造价。

sentences.en: you think of the visual complexity of the device and the expense of the device.
sentences.zh: 但为什么这个经过高度工程设计、视觉上很有吸引力、很昂贵的设备

sentences.en: But why is the sound that's generated by this highly engineered,
sentences.zh: 所产生的声音却如此糟糕呢？

sentences.en: visually attractive, expensive device so poor?
sentences.zh: 它通常是从连接在设备上的一个非常便宜的扬声器里发出来的。

sentences.en: It usually comes out of a very cheap speaker attached to the device.
sentences.zh: 我希望所有医疗设备的警报音至少不是刺耳的，

sentences.en: I'd love all the medical device alarm tones to be at least not dissonant,
sentences.zh: 至少彼此之间是和谐的。

sentences.en: at least in harmony with each other.
sentences.zh: 这其实并没有那么难。

sentences.en: And that's not that difficult.
sentences.zh: 作为一名音乐家，这就好比，我难道不能至少给它们调个音吗？

sentences.en: As a musician, it's like, can I just tune them at least?
sentences.zh: 但横山阳子并不是唯一一个用音乐方法来应对警报疲劳的人。

sentences.en: But Yoko isn't the only one taking a musical approach to alarm fatigue.
sentences.zh: 但横山阳子并不是唯一个以音乐方式来应对警报疲劳的人。

sentences.en: Joe may be an anesthesiologist, but he's also a professional jazz musician.
sentences.zh: 乔伊可能是一名麻醉医师，但他同时也是一位职业爵士音乐家。

sentences.en: It's infuriating, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这真让人抓狂，不是吗？

sentences.en: This is him playing the piano right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是他现在弹钢琴的样子。

sentences.en: I had been playing the piano since I was five years old.
sentences.zh: 我从五岁起就开始弹钢琴了。

sentences.en: So music and medicine was part of my life together for a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以音乐和医学很长一段时间以来都是我生活的一部分。

sentences.en: Right now, alarms are loud and annoying, but they don't have to be.
sentences.zh: 现在，警报声响亮又烦人，但其实完全可以不用这样。

sentences.en: They just have to be different from all the other sounds in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 它们只需要与医院里的所有其他声音有所不同就行。

sentences.en: Imagine that somebody down the hall were to scream.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，走廊那头有人在尖叫。

sentences.en: And it's not loud, but you can perceive it.
sentences.zh: 声音虽然不大，但你能感知到。

sentences.en: We have our attention diverted, not because of the volume,
sentences.zh: 我们的注意力被分散，不是因为音量大小，

sentences.en: but because of the acoustic features of the human scream.
sentences.zh: 而是因为人类尖叫声的声学特征。

sentences.en: There's an acoustic feature called roughness,
sentences.zh: 有一种被称为粗糙度的声学特征，

sentences.en: which has enhanced sensitivity in the amygdala.
sentences.zh: 它能增强杏仁核的敏感度。

sentences.en: So we have this reflexive response.
sentences.zh: 因此我们会产生这种反射性的反应。

sentences.en: This has a surprising implication for our alarm tones.
sentences.zh: 这对我们的警报音有着令人惊讶的启发意义。

sentences.en: Alarms can be softer than background noise,
sentences.zh: 警报声可以比背景噪音更轻柔，

sentences.en: and you can still perceive them.
sentences.zh: 而你依然能够察觉到它们。

sentences.en: A lot of the alarms have what's called a flat amplitude envelope.
sentences.zh: 许多警报声都有所谓的平坦振幅包络。

sentences.en: And so if you imagine the emergency broadcast signal that you hear on TV,
sentences.zh: 如果你想象一下你在电视上听到的紧急广播信号，

sentences.en: that's a flat amplitude envelope,
sentences.zh: 那就是平坦的振幅包络，

sentences.en: and that's an unnatural sound in our environment.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们环境中一种不自然的声音。

sentences.en: The unnatural sound is effective at grabbing our attention.
sentences.zh: 这种不自然的声音在吸引我们注意力方面很有效。

sentences.en: But in a hospital, these unnatural sounds layer on top of each other,
sentences.zh: 但在医院里，这些不自然的声音层层叠加，

sentences.en: creating a wall of sound that we tune out.
sentences.zh: 形成了一道让我们选择忽视的声音墙。

sentences.en: They also create a stress response that's harming our minds and bodies.
sentences.zh: 它们还会产生损害我们身心健康的压力反应。

sentences.en: Compare that with what's called a percussive amplitude envelope,
sentences.zh: 把它与所谓的打击乐振幅包络作个对比，

sentences.en: which has an exponential decay.
sentences.zh: 它具有指数衰减的特点。

sentences.en: So think about if you're clinking two wine glasses together.
sentences.zh: 可以想想你把两个高脚玻璃杯碰在一起时的声音。

sentences.en: That's a sharp upstroke with an exponential decay,
sentences.zh: 那是一个急剧上升后呈指数衰减的声音，

sentences.en: and that's a sound we have in nature.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们在大自然中能听到的声音。

sentences.en: By changing the amplitude envelope to something more natural,
sentences.zh: 通过将振幅包络改变得更加自然，

sentences.en: you can go from this to this.
sentences.zh: 你就能从这种声音变成这种声音。

sentences.en: But even this sound doesn't tell you a lot.
sentences.zh: 但即使是这种声音也没有传达太多信息。

sentences.en: The alarms need to be more informative.
sentences.zh: 警报需要具备更多信息量。

sentences.en: What we are particularly working on is how to contain information in sound,
sentences.zh: 我们目前特别致力于研究如何在声音中包含信息，

sentences.en: and that is what we call auditory icons.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所说的听觉图标。

sentences.en: For example, having a lub-dub heartbeat type of sound
sentences.zh: 例如，在警报中加入类似“咚哒”的心跳声，

sentences.en: in an alarm that is indicative of a cardiovascular problem.
sentences.zh: 以此来指示心血管方面的问题。

sentences.en: The result is something that can tell you exactly what's wrong
sentences.zh: 其结果是，能够在你进入房间之前，

sentences.en: before you enter the room.
sentences.zh: 准确告诉你哪里出了问题。

sentences.en: And that's just the beginning.
sentences.zh: 而这仅仅是个开始。

sentences.en: I don't want to know just when something is bad.
sentences.zh: 我不想只在情况变糟时才知道。

sentences.en: I want to know when something is trending towards being bad.
sentences.zh: 我希望在情况有变糟的趋势时就能知道。

sentences.en: I want visual signals that are always in my receptive field
sentences.zh: 我想要始终在我的接收视野内的视觉信号，

sentences.en: versus a monitor that right now I have to be staring at it.
sentences.zh: 而不是像现在这样必须盯着监视器看。

sentences.en: I want vibratactile information that is wearable and comfortable.
sentences.zh: 我想要可穿戴且舒适的触觉震动信息。

sentences.en: And I want it to provide signals that are not so strong
sentences.zh: 并且我希望它提供的信号不要太强烈，

sentences.en: that I get fatigue or habituated to it.
sentences.zh: 以免让我产生疲劳或适应麻木。

sentences.en: And I want auditory information that is directed to me.
sentences.zh: 我希望获得针对我个人的听觉信息。

sentences.en: When I get auditory information,
sentences.zh: 当我获得听觉信息时，

sentences.en: it's information that can mean something
sentences.zh: 这些信息是有意义的，

sentences.en: and that I need to act upon it.
sentences.zh: 并且是我需要采取行动去处理的。

sentences.en: And we can use the hospital soundscape to do even more.
sentences.zh: 我们可以利用医院的声音景观做到更多。

sentences.en: Researchers are finding ways to give a voice
sentences.zh: 研究人员正在寻找方法，为那些失去声音的人

sentences.en: to people who have lost theirs.
sentences.zh: 赋予声音。

sentences.en: You think of a patient in the ICU when they're non-communicative
sentences.zh: 你可以想想ICU里那些无法交流的病人，

sentences.en: or in long-term acute care,
sentences.zh: 或者长期接受急性护理的病人，

sentences.en: those patients often get neglected.
sentences.zh: 这些病人往往会被忽视。

sentences.en: But they have ways to communicate in a non-traditional sense,
sentences.zh: 但他们有非传统意义上的交流方式，

sentences.en: for example, through their autonomic nervous system.
sentences.zh: 例如通过他们的自主神经系统。

sentences.en: Patients who can't speak or communicate their feelings
sentences.zh: 无法说话或表达自己感受的患者，

sentences.en: are still expressing themselves
sentences.zh: 依然在通过他们的心率或体温

sentences.en: through their heart rate or their body temperature.
sentences.zh: 来表达自我。

sentences.en: So they're communicating, but not in a traditional verbal sense.
sentences.zh: 所以他们一直在交流，只是方式并非传统的语言交流。

sentences.en: How can we take those physiologic signals,
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能获取这些生理信号，

sentences.en: turn them into sound in a way that we can start
sentences.zh: 以某种方式将它们转化为声音，从而开始

sentences.en: to ascertain what these patients, what these people are saying?
sentences.zh: 弄清楚这些病人和这些人究竟在表达什么？

sentences.en: The result is something called biomusic,
sentences.zh: 其结果就是所谓的生物音乐，

sentences.en: pioneered by a colleague of Joe's at McGill University in Montreal.
sentences.zh: 由乔伊在蒙特利尔麦吉尔大学的一位同事率先开创。

sentences.en: Sensors on the patient's body detect vital signs,
sentences.zh: 患者身体上的传感器检测生命体征，

sentences.en: and that makes the data into sound.
sentences.zh: 并以此将数据转化为声音。

sentences.en: Heart rate controls the tempo,
sentences.zh: 心率控制节奏，

sentences.en: temperature determines the notes,
sentences.zh: 体温决定音符，

sentences.en: and skin sweat drives the melody.
sentences.zh: 皮肤出汗驱动旋律。

sentences.en: The result is actually kind of beautiful.
sentences.zh: 最终的效果其实还挺美妙的。

sentences.en: Biomusic is being looked at as a way
sentences.zh: 生物音乐正被视作一种途径，

sentences.en: for non-verbal autistic children to express themselves.
sentences.zh: 帮助非语言表达的孤独症儿童表达自我。

sentences.en: Here's a calm state of mind,
sentences.zh: 这里展示的是平静的心态，

sentences.en: and here's an anxious one.
sentences.zh: 而这里是焦虑的心态。

sentences.en: You don't have to be a medical specialist
sentences.zh: 你不需要成为医学专家

sentences.en: to hear the difference.
sentences.zh: 就能听出其中的区别。

sentences.en: Our hope is that we can make it easy to implement
sentences.zh: 我们的希望是，能让它在全世界轻松落地实施，

sentences.en: throughout the world,
sentences.zh: 在世界各地，

sentences.en: where you don't have to be at a
sentences.zh: 你无需身处拥有高档脑电图设备的

sentences.en: high-powered academic institution
sentences.zh: 顶尖学术机构，

sentences.en: with fancy EEG equipment
sentences.zh: 借助精密的高档脑电图设备

sentences.en: to make this a reality.
sentences.zh: 就能让这一切成为现实。

sentences.en: Joel Beckerman believes our hospital soundscapes
sentences.zh: 乔尔·贝克曼认为，我们的医院声音景观

sentences.en: can be improved,
sentences.zh: 可以得到改善，

sentences.en: from an unhealthy and dangerous cacophony
sentences.zh: 从不健康且危险的嘈杂声

sentences.en: to something more useful and healthy.
sentences.zh: 转变为更有用、更健康的声音。

sentences.en: Imagine you could walk into a room
sentences.zh: 想象一下，你可以走进一个房间，

sentences.en: and be able to sift through enormous data sets
sentences.zh: 仅仅通过声音就能筛选出海量的数据集。

sentences.en: by sound alone.
sentences.zh: 仅凭声音。

sentences.en: We actually create an idealized soundscape
sentences.zh: 我们实际上为未来医院病房中的

sentences.en: for what a sonification of data idea might be
sentences.zh: 数据声化构想创造了一个理想的声音景观。

sentences.en: in a hospital room of the future.
sentences.zh: 在未来的医院病房里。

sentences.en: Basically, I think he's in good shape.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我认为他的情况很好。

sentences.en: Maybe in a week,
sentences.zh: 也许在一周后，

sentences.en: we can look at the chart again and make sure.
sentences.zh: 我们可以再次查看病历以作确认。

sentences.en: Sounds good.
sentences.zh: 听起来不错。

sentences.en: You don't need to be a musician.
sentences.zh: 你不需要成为音乐家。

sentences.en: You don't need to be really intensely trained for this.
sentences.zh: 你不需要为此接受过非常密集的训练。

sentences.en: You can determine whether a pitch is higher than another
sentences.zh: 如果音高相差足够远，

sentences.en: or lower than another if they're pretty far apart.
sentences.zh: 你就能判断出一个音高是比另一个高还是低。

sentences.en: You can determine whether a sound is rising
sentences.zh: 你能判断出一个声音是在上升

sentences.en: or a sound is falling.
sentences.zh: 还是在下降。

sentences.en: In a very, very short period of time,
sentences.zh: 在非常非常短的时间内，

sentences.en: we can help people understand those differences
sentences.zh: 我们可以帮助人们理解这些差异，

sentences.en: of all the different key healthcare data points
sentences.zh: 涵盖所有不同的关键医疗数据点，

sentences.en: to understand what a patient needs
sentences.zh: 从而了解患者需要什么，

sentences.en: or whether that patient is okay
sentences.zh: 或者患者是否安好，

sentences.en: and they can turn their attention elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 然后他们可以把注意力转移到别的事情上去。

sentences.en: When I was in music school,
sentences.zh: 当我还在音乐学校时，

sentences.en: my piano teacher told me,
sentences.zh: 我的钢琴老师告诉我，

sentences.en: the more you actively listen to jazz
sentences.zh: 你越是积极地聆听爵士乐

sentences.en: and you practice,
sentences.zh: 并勤加练习，

sentences.en: you're adding colors to your palate.
sentences.zh: 你的调色盘里就越是会添上更多色彩。

sentences.en: The more I study, the more I practice,
sentences.zh: 我学习得越多，练习得越多，

sentences.en: the more I listen,
sentences.zh: 聆听得越多，

sentences.en: I have more colors on my palate.
sentences.zh: 我调色盘里的色彩就越丰富。

sentences.en: I can create a beautiful painting.
sentences.zh: 我就能创作出一幅美丽的画作。

sentences.en: And so the reason why we need to do this
sentences.zh: 因此，我们之所以需要这样做，

sentences.en: is because this adds colors to our palate.
sentences.zh: 是因为这为我们的调色盘增添了色彩。

sentences.en: And I think it's important
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，从患者护理的角度来看，

sentences.en: from a patient care perspective
sentences.zh: 从患者护理的角度来看

sentences.en: that we make the most beautiful painting
sentences.zh: 创作出我们所能画出的最美丽的画作

sentences.en: that we can create.
sentences.zh: 是至关重要的。
